title: Total Knee and Total Hip Arthroplasty Rehabilitation
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Explain the plan, practise exercises and walking aids before surgery, assess home (stairs, toilet height, support). Pre-operative exercise may modestly improve early function [Ref – to verify].
working: Total Knee and Total Hip Arthroplasty Rehabilitation
qa: Why mobilise on the day of surgery or day 1? Reduces complications and speeds recovery.
Which motion is commonly hardest to regain after TKA? Flexion, and full extension if not prioritised.
What is a sign of hip abductor weakness? Trendelenburg gait.
Why do precautions differ between patients after THA? They depend on surgical approach and surgeon preference.
Sudden hip pain with shortened leg after bending? Suspected dislocation.

redFlags.Finding: Sudden hip pain, leg shortened and rotated after a movement (THA)
Calf pain and swelling, sudden breathlessness
Knee flexion not improving by the early weeks after TKA
redFlags.Action: Inform surgeon; manipulation under anaesthesia may be considered

modalityNotes: Ice and compression for swelling and pain. NMES for quadriceps after TKA may help early strength [Ref – to verify].
